messages:
maria: New customer Vectra Labs completed OIDC SSO but no API credential showed up in their project. Console says "Provisioning queued" and the UI never moves to "Active key". Can someone take a look?
ajay: Thanks — can you paste the customer org id + project id? I can check the provisioner logs.
maria: org=vectra-628, project=vectra-prod. Provisioner trace id: pv-2026-11-03-7f9a. UX shows banner: "Credential queued for creation (pending claim)".
provisioner-bot: [provisioner event] claim_received id=pv-2026-11-03-7f9a status=queued -> worker_assigned
ajay: Looking at the provisioner service, I see the claim was accepted but the downstream createKey call returned 202 and never completed:
```
2026-11-03T14:12:21Z INFO claim pv-2026-11-03-7f9a accepted
2026-11-03T14:12:21Z DEBUG calling iam-service /createKey org=vectra-628 project=vectra-prod
2026-11-03T14:12:21Z WARN iam-service responded 202 Accepted {"operationId":"op-9b3c"}
2026-11-03T14:12:21Z INFO polling operation op-9b3c -> status=IN_PROGRESS
2026-11-03T14:15:21Z ERROR operation op-9b3c timed out after 3m, marking claim failed? but status not set
```
maria: UI doesn't show a failure state, just stuck queued forever. Customer is blocked from calling the API.
ajay: Hmm the timeout path here is weird — it should mark the claim failed and surface an error. I'll check the operation-poller. @liz_ops can you check the operations queue and whether op-9b3c is still in DB or Redis?
liz_ops: On it. Quick check: op-9b3c exists in ops-table but status is null. No retry scheduled. I see a worker crash around 14:15 in the autoscaler logs, restart happened. Might be a race where the poller didn't update status after restart.
sam_eng: If the poller crashed mid-update it could leave the claim in limbo. We have a known edge case when the op record is left with null status. Need a repair job to reconcile ops without terminal status older than TTL.
maria: Customer needs an ETA. Any workaround we can do to surface a key manually?
ajay: We can manually call the internal createKey endpoint with the same payload and then patch the claim status, but that requires an ops run and audit entry.
liz_ops: I'll run a manual reconcile for pv-2026-11-03-7f9a now: querying op-9b3c, then invoking createKey with idempotency token. I will paste the command I run:
```
# internal one-shot (ops only)
curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/provision/createKey \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"org":"vectra-628","project":"vectra-prod","claim_id":"pv-2026-11-03-7f9a","idempotency":"op-9b3c"}'
```
provisioner-bot: [provisioner event] reconcile started claim=pv-2026-11-03-7f9a by=liz_ops
ajay: After manual createKey, we should update claim to status=active and attach the key to the project. Also create an incident note and customer-facing message.
liz_ops: Manual run completed — createKey returned 201 key_id=key-vct-5f2a. Claim patched to active. UI now shows the key in console. Leaving a follow-up to fix the poller crash.
maria: Thanks! I messaged the customer with the key and included the temporary note. They were relieved.
sam_eng: I'll open a PR to add a reconciliation cron that scans ops table for operations older than 1m with non-terminal status and requeues them. Also adding a metric and alert for operations left in null status.
ajay: Filing a postmortem action: PM/infra to triage autoscaler worker crash and add defensive writes. Ticket: INT-5429.
maria: Marking this resolved for customer; tagging INT-5429 for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
provisioner-bot: [audit] manual_reconcile claim=pv-2026-11-03-7f9a by=liz_ops reason=customer_blocker
